entities.name: Leptospirosis
entities.description: A life-threatening biphasic zoonotic infection caused by pathogenic spirochetes of the genus Leptospira, characterized by an acute leptospiremic phase with fever, conjunctival suffusion, and calf tenderness, potentially progressing to severe icteric Weil disease (jaundice, acute renal failure, hemorrhage) or catastrophic severe pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome.

entities.name: Rodent Urine Contaminated Floodwaters or Soil
entities.description: Environmental surface water, wet mud, soil, or urban floodwaters contaminated with urine from chronically colonized rodents, serving as the primary vehicle for percutaneous or permucosal transmission during monsoons and flooding.

entities.name: Asymptomatic Rodent Maintenance Hosts
entities.description: Brown and black rats (Rattus norvegicus, Rattus rattus) and field mice that maintain chronic asymptomatic colonization of renal proximal tubules and shed massive quantities of viable Leptospira spirochetes in their urine indefinitely.

entities.name: Occupational and Recreational Freshwater Inoculation
entities.description: High-risk percutaneous or permucosal exposure through occupational tasks (sewer cleaning, rice farming, abattoir work) or freshwater immersion sports (rafting, canoeing, triathlon) involving contact with contaminated water.

entities.name: Leptospira interrogans
entities.description: Pathogenic obligate aerobic, highly motile spirochete of the genus Leptospira comprising over 250 distinct serovars across >24 serogroups, which invades host tissues, disseminates hematogenously, and causes extensive microvascular endothelial injury.

entities.name: Conjunctival Suffusion Without Inflammatory Exudate
entities.description: Bilateral ciliary and bulbar conjunctival erythema and vascular engorgement appearing on days 3–4 of illness, characteristically devoid of purulent discharge, crusting, or chemosis, serving as a pathognomonic physical hallmark in 60–85% of cases.

entities.name: Severe Gastrocnemius Calf Muscle Tenderness
entities.description: Disproportionate, excruciating myalgia and intense tenderness localized to the calf (gastrocnemius and soleus) and lumbar paraspinal muscles, often rendering the patient unable to walk or tolerate light manual palpation.

entities.name: Weil Disease Triad of Jaundice Renal Failure and Hemorrhage
entities.description: Severe icteric leptospirosis occurring in 5–15% of patients, manifested by the life-threatening triad of deep bronze-colored jaundice, rapid acute kidney injury, and hemorrhagic diathesis.

entities.name: Severe Pulmonary Hemorrhagic Syndrome
entities.description: Catastrophic intra-alveolar hemorrhage secondary to toxin-mediated pulmonary capillary endothelial damage, presenting with sudden dyspnea, hemoptysis, and hypoxic respiratory failure with mortality exceeding 50%.

entities.name: Biphasic Fever with Shaking Chills
entities.description: Abrupt onset of high remittent or continuous fever (39–40°C) accompanied by violent shaking chills, diaphoresis, and severe frontal/retro-orbital headache during the initial leptospiremic phase (days 1–7).

entities.name: High Total Bilirubin with Disproportionately Mild Transaminitis
entities.description: Marked conjugated hyperbilirubinemia (total bilirubin 10–30 mg/dL) reflecting canalicular cholestasis, accompanied by only mild-to-moderate transaminase elevations (AST and ALT 100–300 U/L, rarely >5x ULN, virtually never >1,000 U/L).

entities.name: Early Hypokalemic or Normokalemic Acute Kidney Injury
entities.description: Rapidly rising serum creatinine and BUN that presents uniquely in early stages as polyuric or non-oliguric hypokalemic/normokalemic renal failure due to spirochetal toxin inhibition of apical Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransporters in the loop of Henle.

entities.name: Marked Neutrophilic Leukocytosis with Bandemia
entities.description: Total peripheral white blood cell count of 12,000–25,000/uL with >80% neutrophils and >10% bands (or leukemoid reactions >30,000/uL in severe Weil disease), markedly distinguishing leptospirosis from arboviral leukopenia.

entities.name: Severe Thrombocytopenia with High C-Reactive Protein
entities.description: Platelet count <100,000/uL (frequently <50,000/uL in severe pulmonary or renal failure) paired with profound elevation of inflammatory markers (CRP >100–200 mg/L and high ESR) reflecting systemic vasculitis and microvascular injury.

entities.name: Markedly Elevated Serum Creatine Kinase
entities.description: Total serum creatine kinase elevated >5–10 times the upper limit of normal in >50% of patients at presentation, resulting from intense skeletal muscle necrosis and rhabdomyolysis.

entities.name: Diffuse Snowflake Alveolar Infiltrates on Chest Radiography
entities.description: Bedside chest radiograph showing bilateral patchy, non-segmental alveolar infiltrates or diffuse nodular 'snowstorm / snowflake' opacities predominantly affecting the middle and lower zones, indicating alveolar hemorrhage.

entities.name: Nephromegaly with Acalculous Gallbladder Wall Edema on Bedside Ultrasound
entities.description: Abdominal ultrasound demonstrating bilateral enlarged kidneys with increased cortical echogenicity and acalculous gallbladder wall edema, while confirming normal, non-dilated intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts.

entities.name: Presence of Purulent Conjunctival Exudate
entities.description: Copious purulent or mucopurulent ocular discharge, conjunctival crusting, or marked chemosis, which contradicts the classic dry vascular ciliary injection of leptospiral conjunctival suffusion.

entities.name: Severe Transaminitis with AST or ALT Exceeding 2000 U/L
entities.description: Serum AST or ALT elevations exceeding 1,000–2,000 U/L, which indicates massive acute hepatocellular necrosis (typical of viral or toxic hepatitis) rather than the cholestatic transaminitis of leptospirosis.

entities.name: Leukopenia with WBC Count Under 4000 per Microliter
entities.description: Normal or depressed total peripheral white blood cell count (<4,000/uL) in the presence of acute febrile jaundice and renal failure, arguing strongly against acute leptospirosis.

entities.name: Biliary Ductal Dilation on Ultrasound
entities.description: Ultrasonographic evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary duct dilation or choledocholithiasis, establishing mechanical extrahepatic biliary obstruction.

entities.name: Presence of Intraerythrocytic Parasites on Blood Smear
entities.description: Microscopic visualization of intraerythrocytic Plasmodium trophozoites, schizonts, or gametocytes on Giemsa-stained blood smears, confirming malaria as the etiology.

entities.name: Acute Viral Hepatitis
entities.description: Acute viral hepatitis (HAV, HBV, HEV) causing jaundice, anorexia, and tender hepatomegaly.

entities.name: Dengue Fever
entities.description: Arboviral infection presenting with acute high fever, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, severe thrombocytopenia, and plasma leakage.

entities.name: Acute Bacterial Cholangitis
entities.description: Ascending biliary infection presenting with Charcot's triad (fever, jaundice, right upper quadrant pain) due to biliary ductal obstruction.

entities.name: Severe Falciparum Malaria
entities.description: Life-threatening parasitic infection caused by Plasmodium falciparum presenting with cyclical fevers, rigors, hemolytic jaundice, and renal failure.

entities.name: Intravenous Penicillin G or Ceftriaxone Therapy
entities.description: Parenteral bactericidal therapy with high-dose intravenous Penicillin G (1.5 million units IV q6h) or Ceftriaxone (1–2 g IV daily) for 7 days, which significantly curtails fever duration and halts progression of renal failure when initiated early.

entities.name: Oral Doxycycline or Azithromycin Therapy
entities.description: Oral antimicrobial regimen (Doxycycline 100 mg BID or Azithromycin) for mild outpatient leptospirosis, leading to prompt defervescence and cessation of urinary leptospiral shedding.

entities.name: Jarisch-Herxheimer Reaction Following First Antibiotic Dose
entities.description: Acute clinical exacerbation occurring in 10–20% of patients within 2–6 hours of the first parenteral antibiotic dose, characterized by sudden rigors, temperature spike, and transient hypotension resulting from massive spirochetal lysis.

entities.name: Ineffective Antimicrobial Monotherapy Without Organ Support in Weil Syndrome
entities.description: Antimicrobial therapy alone fails to avert mortality in advanced Weil disease or severe pulmonary hemorrhage without timely renal replacement therapy (hemodialysis) and lung-protective mechanical ventilation.

relationships.target: Rodent Urine Contaminated Floodwaters or Soil
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Transmission occurs via percutaneous or permucosal exposure to floodwaters, mud, wet soil, or surface water contaminated with urine shed by chronically colonized rodents (Rattus norvegicus, Rattus rattus).

[TRANSMITTED_BY] Primary reservoir maintenance hosts are rodents that excrete astronomical quantities of viable Leptospira spirochetes into the environment indefinitely without developing clinical disease.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Agricultural workers (rice/sugarcane), sewage laborers, and freshwater recreational athletes experience percutaneous or permucosal inoculation during environmental water exposure.

[HAS_PATHOGEN] Caused by pathogenic spirochetes of the genus Leptospira, predominantly Leptospira interrogans, which disseminate hematogenously during the septicemic phase and invade renal tubules, liver parenchyma, and capillary endothelium.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Present in 60–85% of cases on days 3–4, presenting as bilateral intense ciliary flush devoid of purulent secretions or conjunctival crusting, representing a distinctive diagnostic physical hallmark.
[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Severe, disproportionate myalgia localized to the gastrocnemius calf and lumbar paraspinal muscles is a classic hallmark of early leptospiremic phase disease.

relationships.target: Weil Disease Triad of Jaundice Renal Failure and Hemorrhage
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Life-threatening icteric syndrome manifested by deep bronze/orange jaundice, rapid acute kidney injury, and diathetic hemorrhage.
[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Catastrophic manifestation of leptospirosis featuring extensive capillary endothelial injury leading to intra-alveolar bleeding and lethal hypoxic respiratory failure.
[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Abrupt onset of high spiking fever accompanied by violent shaking chills, diaphoresis, and severe cephalalgia representing initial bacteremic dissemination.

relationships.target: High Total Bilirubin with Disproportionately Mild Transaminitis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Serum total/direct bilirubin is markedly elevated with dramatic jaundice, while transaminases (AST/ALT) remain disproportionately modest (<300–400 U/L), sharply distinguishing leptospirosis from hepatocellular necrosis.

relationships.target: Early Hypokalemic or Normokalemic Acute Kidney Injury
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Acute kidney injury presenting with preserved urine output and normal or low serum potassium levels due to impaired tubular sodium and potassium reabsorption.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Prominent neutrophilic leukocytosis with significant left shift and toxic granulation is universally evident at initial hospital triage.

relationships.target: Severe Thrombocytopenia with High C-Reactive Protein
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Concomitant severe thrombocytopenia alongside extreme elevations of acute phase reactants (CRP >100 mg/L) reflects intense systemic inflammation and endothelial disruption.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Substantial elevation of creatine kinase reflects direct skeletal muscle injury and ongoing myositis/rhabdomyolysis.

relationships.target: Diffuse Snowflake Alveolar Infiltrates on Chest Radiography
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission chest radiograph displaying bilateral patchy snowflake nodular opacities indicative of intra-alveolar hemorrhage.

relationships.target: Nephromegaly with Acalculous Gallbladder Wall Edema on Bedside Ultrasound
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Abdominal sonography demonstrates bilateral nephromegaly and acalculous gallbladder wall thickening while explicitly confirming normal, non-dilated biliary ducts.
[RULED_OUT_BY] The presence of purulent or copious inflammatory conjunctival exudate strongly argues against leptospirosis, whose cardinal hallmark is pure non-purulent conjunctival suffusion.

relationships.target: Severe Transaminitis with AST or ALT Exceeding 2000 U/L
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] AST or ALT elevations above 2,000 U/L effectively exclude uncomplicated leptospirosis, where hepatic involvement produces striking cholestatic jaundice with transaminases typically below 400 U/L.

relationships.target: Leukopenia with WBC Count Under 4000 per Microliter
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Total white blood cell count <4,000/uL in the presence of severe febrile jaundice and renal impairment strongly excludes leptospirosis, which consistently provokes marked neutrophilic leukocytosis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Sonographic evidence of dilated intra- or extrahepatic biliary ducts or choledocholithiasis rules out leptospirosis in favor of acute mechanical or bacterial cholangitis.

relationships.target: Presence of Intraerythrocytic Parasites on Blood Smear
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Identification of intraerythrocytic Plasmodium species on blood film confirms malaria as the source of hemolysis, rigors, and jaundice rather than leptospirosis.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leptospirosis is differentiated from acute viral hepatitis by the presence of marked neutrophilic leukocytosis, elevated serum creatine kinase, acute renal injury, conjunctival suffusion, and transaminases <400 U/L, whereas viral hepatitis exhibits transaminases >1,000–5,000 U/L and normal renal function.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leptospirosis is differentiated from dengue fever by profound neutrophilic leukocytosis, marked direct hyperbilirubinemia, severe calf tenderness, and highly elevated CRP (>100 mg/L), whereas dengue features prominent leukopenia (<4,000/uL), hemoconcentration, normal bilirubin, and low CRP.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leptospirosis is differentiated from acute bacterial cholangitis by completely normal, non-dilated bile ducts on abdominal ultrasound, prominent non-purulent conjunctival suffusion, and disproportionate calf tenderness.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leptospirosis is differentiated from severe falciparum malaria by predominantly direct (conjugated) hyperbilirubinemia, absence of intraerythrocytic parasites on blood smear, and presence of bilateral conjunctival suffusion and calf pain, whereas malaria causes indirect (unconjugated) hemolytic jaundice with elevated LDH.

relationships.target: Intravenous Penicillin G or Ceftriaxone Therapy
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Severe leptospirosis responds promptly to intravenous penicillin G or ceftriaxone; early administration within the first 4–7 days of symptom onset significantly accelerates defervescence and halts progression of organ failure.
[RESPONDS_TO] Mild outpatient leptospirosis responds rapidly to a 7-day course of oral doxycycline or azithromycin, shortening illness duration and eliminating urinary spirochete shedding.

relationships.target: Jarisch-Herxheimer Reaction Following First Antibiotic Dose
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Development of a Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction (rigors, fever spike, hypotension) within 2–6 hours of antibiotic initiation serves as a diagnostic therapeutic clue reflecting massive bactericidal lysis of spirochetes.

relationships.target: Ineffective Antimicrobial Monotherapy Without Organ Support in Weil Syndrome
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Antibiotic therapy alone without aggressive supportive management (early renal replacement therapy, mechanical ventilation for SPHS) fails to curtail mortality in advanced multi-organ failure.
